summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for dyspnea and chest pain due to hypervolemia and acute on chronic renal failure. She developed flash pulmonary edema likely triggered by atrial fibrillation, requiring intubation and mechanical ventilation. Dialysis and ultrafiltration improved her respiratory status. She had pancytopenia attributed to medications including linezolid and ranitidine, which were discontinued; blood counts subsequently recovered. A kidney transplant biopsy was performed, showing chronic inflammation and scarring, with final pathology pending. Her atrial fibrillation was managed with amiodarone and increased metoprolol, though INR remained subtherapeutic at discharge. She expressed a desire to discuss transplant removal with her nephrologist and surgeon due to recurrent infections and ongoing complications. She was discharged home in stable condition with medication adjustments and close follow-up planned.
